playbook:
When I file a claim after firing, I always claim the true result the office told me — the rules say claims must match the private result, so lying about a miss is wasted effort and possibly punished, and my false "hit" claims gained me nothing.

When the escort stage comes, I treat it as the biggest scoring lever: mutual escort pays 5 points each, dwarfing the 4 points for a hit. I use my station note early to propose a mutual escort pairing (e.g., "Echo will escort Foxtrot if Foxtrot escorts Echo"), then name that boat every round and keep naming it even through silence — consistency is what makes pairing possible. I never answer [salvage: none] when any boat has signaled willingness to pair; "none" scores zero guaranteed.

When I post a station note, I use it for coordination, not fluff: propose an escort partner, state my intended fire pattern, or signal compliance with what others are doing. When others converge on a phrase like "steady on station," I match it, but I add an escort proposal on top rather than just echoing.

When I choose a fire target, I follow the standing order and never fire on Harbor — the 3-point jettison gain is not worth being put off the board, and the scoreboard shows an early Harbor shot left me stuck at 0.

When I pick a fire cell, I aim at the middle of the grid (4–6) where opponents are most likely to hide, and I track where my target hid in prior rounds from the public hit record rather than firing the extreme cells (1, 9), which are low-probability.

When I hide, I avoid the cell I was just hit in and avoid repeating my own previous hide; I rotate through mid cells with occasional edge moves, since opponents who hit me tend to fire nearby next round.

When choosing between deception and truth anywhere the office validates my input, I choose truth — the validation rules mean deception only works in notes and escort choices, and that is where I should spend any misdirection, not in claims.

My baseline target each game: lock a mutual escort every round for +5/round, take expected hits from standing-order fire as a bonus, and accept being shot at as the cost of a predictable schedule.

1.text:
When a claim is put to me, I file the true result every time. The rules say claims must match the private result, and when I bluffed a hit on a confirmed miss I gained nothing — honesty is both safe and free of risk.

When the fire stage comes, I follow the standing order and shoot my assigned next station; I never fire on Harbor unless I am far ahead and can absorb retaliation, because its threat to put me off the board ends my scoring entirely, and the 3-point payroll jettison is a poor trade against losing all future shots.

When I fire, I pick my target's most likely cell from the shot history and notes rather than my own favorite numbers; I track which cells each opponent has hidden in and aim where a pattern repeats, and I break my own pattern so nobody can do the same to me.

When the hide stage comes, I never reuse a cell I was hit in or that the boat shooting at me keeps guessing; if an opponent has connected on me recently, I jump to an unexploited edge cell rather than staying near my previous spots.

I never copy my fire cell from my hide cell or use the same number for both in a round; diversifying keeps my opponent's reads from beating me in two places at once.

When the escort stage comes, the 5-point mutual payout dwarfs everything else, so I always file an escort claim and use my note earlier in the round to propose a pairing ("I'll name you, name me") to the boat least likely to betray it, then honor the deal. Naming "none" every round left large points on the table and was my biggest missed opportunity.

When posting notes, I use them as the coordination channel: propose escort swaps, signal my intended hide range vaguely to misdirect, and keep a calm cooperative tone so partners trust my escort claims.

I never rely on a single lucky hit as my plan; a 4-point final score built on shots alone is fragile, so from round one I stack escort income on top of the standing-order shooting.

Late in the patrol, if I am ahead, I take safe honest plays; if behind, I escalate only via coordinated escorts, never via Harbor raids that get me removed from the board.

2.text:
- Never fire on Harbor unless the 3-point swing clearly wins me the game in the final round; the retaliation threat (off the board) is not worth it earlier.
- Claims must match the private result — do not file a false hit. It violates the enforceable rule, wastes nothing for the opponent, and damages my credibility for note-based coordination. I did this and it gained me nothing.
- The escort payoff (5 points each for mutual naming) dwarfs shooting (4 for a hit, -1 to be hit). My top priority every game is to set up a mutual escort pair as fast as possible.
- When the note stage comes, do not write "steady on station" — that wastes the channel. Use notes to propose or confirm an escort pact: name the boat I will escort and ask them to name me back. I ignored notes entirely and finished at -1 while escorts went unclaimed.
- When choosing whom to escort, pick the boat that signaled agreement in notes; if none did, escort the boat most likely to reciprocate next round (the one I haven't shot, or the current leader's rival) and say so in my note.
- Once a mutual escort pair is paying out, never break it — 5 points per round beats any shot. Repeat the same escort claim every round.
- When firing, obey the standing-order target (defying it costs me the pact network's trust) but use notes from the target and its past hit locations to pick the cell. Fire where the target has been hit before or where it has never hidden — avoid cells I already know were misses against it.
- When hiding, never reuse a cell that was just hit, and avoid the cells my predator has recently fired at. Track my predator's sequence and step away from its trend rather than picking "less obvious" numbers at random.
- When behind late, keep the escort income flowing rather than gambling on hits — a guaranteed 5 beats a 1-in-9 shot at 4.
- In the last round, if no escort pact exists and I trail, escort the boat that has escorted me or signaled me most recently; a last-round mutual by luck still pays.
